Shallow slightly elevated near-frontal viewpoint from a standing player's eye looking forward along a flat horizontal corridor, no isometric or diagonal camera. Long horizontal form about 2.2:1, generous margins, whole silhouette in frame. Reference 1 is the stone palette and grain. Reference 2 is adjacent floor material, for color matching only. Ancient matte warm taupe-brown limestone, fine abrasion and chips, subtle diffuse upper-left illumination, medium contrast, dry granular detail. Realistic detailed painted game material, quiet earth colors. No floor surface, external shadow, scene, haze, character, text or border. Subject: a heavy broken horizontal stone column shaft laying left-to-right on its side, split broken end on left and worn ring collar on right, a few small attached chips at the contact line. Low, elongated silhouette, rough eroded cylindrical form and readable broken core. Main shaft is the full width of the sprite, not a collection of detached objects.

narrow.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production first-person labyrinth side exit wall plane decal. Single head-on orthographic stone doorway surround, directly face the wall and keep both jambs vertical, straight on, no corner or projected thickness or camera angle. Portrait 3:4 composition, whole surround visible. Image 1 is the existing labyrinth wall texture and paint reference. Image 2 is limestone color and fine abrasion reference. Weathered warm taupe-brown limestone, chiselled rough hewn blocks, subdued soft diffuse illumination, hand-painted realistic game texture. Crucial: the hole must be a real alpha cutout revealing the same completely transparent backdrop as the exterior; two stone jambs at either side stand on the same horizontal threshold line and the opening extends to the bottom with no stone running across the bottom. No black interior, no door, no material in the opening, no tunnel or scenery inside or outside, no ground, no cast shadow, no text or border. Shape like an upside-down U, open all the way to the bottom. Subject: narrow service access with a visibly slim empty pass-through (about 33% of the finished frame width), weathered stacked block side piers and a sturdy chipped horizontal lintel above a tall rectangular doorway. Keep the doorway sides fairly straight, with just small chips at the edges. Jamb exteriors have rough broken mortar, contained in portrait canvas.
